caveats: This is an unpaired cohort: any case-control difference in sampling or follow-up can confound the score-time association; report how follow-up and event rates compare between arms

steps.question: Does the 20-gene signature score associate with time to event in this 60 case / 60 control cohort, once case vs control status is accounted for (Cox PH: score + condition), and is the association robust to proportional-hazards diagnostics?
steps.description: Fit Cox proportional hazards models of time-to-event on the 20-gene signature score, adjusting for case vs control status, with univariate comparisons and proportional-hazards diagnostics; plot Kaplan-Meier curves stratified by score.
acceptance_criteria: Converged Cox model with signature score and condition, reporting HR per 1-SD score increase, 95% CI, and p-value for score
Schoenfeld-residual PH test reported for both covariates; if violated, an alternative model (stratified or time-varying) is fitted and both results reported
Univariate Cox models for score alone and condition alone included for comparison
Plotted KM curves by median score within cases and within controls; sign and magnitude of association stated explicitly, with the caveat that the cohort is modest (120 samples, ~60 per arm)

plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs time-to-event, Cox adjusted for case/control
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a survival association test, so the plan is two steps. First, the raw Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 120 samples) must be normalized before the 20 signature genes (signature_genes.csv) can be turned into a single per-sample score; this step also aligns counts to the 120-row metadata (condition, time, event) and verifies all signature genes are present. Second, the resulting sample-level table feeds Cox proportional hazards models of time-to-event on the score adjusted for case vs control (60 vs 60, unpaired), with univariate comparisons, Schoenfeld-residual PH diagnostics, and Kaplan-Meier display stratified by score within each arm. A single batch and small feature set keep both steps light; lifelines/scikit-survival cover the survival machinery.

Presence of each of the 20 signature genes in the 12,000-gene matrix is reported; score computed on the genes found (or a stated imputation if a gene is absent)
Output table contains per-sample score, condition, time, and event with no missing values in those columns
Event/time sanity checks reported (non-negative time, event coded 0/1, number of events per group)
